subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS Dashboard embedded browser receive only configured shared gateway tokens/passwords, or may it reuse native device tokens from the app's websocket pairing state?
rationale: The choice affects a credential boundary and existing upgrade behavior, and the repository has two open sibling PRs that implement conflicting policies on the same Dashboard auth surface.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Rebase this PR over current main, update the endpoint-reload path too, and require macOS proof that stored native device tokens are not injected into the browser.

options.title: Allow native-token browser parity
options.body: Close or replace this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction after documenting why browser injection may reuse native device tokens.

options.title: Pause both PRs for design
options.body: Keep both draft branches blocked until the Dashboard auth model is documented and a single replacement PR implements it.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Rebase this PR over current main, update the endpoint-reload path too, and require macOS proof that stored native device tokens are not injected into the browser.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the native Dashboard surface and merged the newer endpoint-reload path that this PR now has to reconcile.
